title: EAF2 Downregulation Recruits Tumor-associated Macrophages in Prostate Cancer
author: Cao, Sun, et al.
materials: LNCaP prostate cancer cells and human THP-1 cells were obtained from the Cell Bank of Type Culture Collection of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (Shanghai, CN) and maintained in RPMI 1640 medium supplemented with 10% FBS and 5% antibiotics. For stable EAF2 knockdown, LNCaP cells were incubated with LV-EAF2-RNAi or negative control (Genechem, CN) for 12 h and then treated with Puromycin(5ug/ml)for one week. For the conditioned media, the indicated cells were incubated with non-serum media for 48 h, and the culture media were collected and centrifuged for further experiments. For THP-1 cells differentiation, THP-1 cells were treated with phorbol myristate acetate (PMA, Sigma, USA) for 30 h to achieve macrophage differentiation(M0). Then M0 macrophages were cultured in the conditioned medium of LNCaP cells with or without EAF2 knockdown in petri dishes for 3 days to determine the effect of prostate cancer cells on the differentiation of M0 macrophages. Add 20ng/mL IL-4 (MCE, CN) and 20ng/mL IL-13 (MCE, CN) to M0 macrophages induced by THP-1 to induce their differentiation into M2 phenotype.

Total RNA was extracted from cells using TRIzol reagent (Invitrogen, USA) and the RNA reverse transcription was proceeded using a first-strand cDNA synthesis kit (Promega, USA). Real-time PCR was carried out using SYBR green mix (Thermo Scientific Waltham, USA). The sequences of primers used were presented below.

steps.title: Select patient cohort
steps.instruction: Select 38 prostate cancer patients who underwent radical prostatectomy, grade them by Gleason score, and divide them into EAF2‑low and EAF2‑high groups for correlation with CD163 immunohistochemistry.

steps.title: Perform immunohistochemistry
steps.instruction: Process prostate cancer sections for IHC, incubate with primary and secondary antibodies, develop staining, and evaluate CD163 positive cells.

substeps.instruction: Deparaffinize tissue sections and perform heat‑induced epitope retrieval (HIER).

Incubate sections for 1 h at room temperature with primary antibodies: EAF2 (1:200, Proteintech, CN), CD4 (original solution, Spincle, CN), CD8 (original solution, Gene Tech, CN), CD68 (original solution, Gene Tech, CN), CD20 (original solution, Gene Tech, CN), and CD163 (1:100, Dako, DK).
Apply GTvision secondary antibody (CN) for 30 min at room temperature.
Develop staining with diaminobenzidine (DAB) and counterstain with hematoxylin.
Have two pathologists independently evaluate staining; count CD163‑positive cells in 5 fields using a blind method and calculate the average.

steps.title: Culture prostate and monocyte cells
steps.instruction: Maintain LNCaP and THP‑1 cells, generate stable EAF2 knockdown, collect conditioned media, differentiate THP‑1 to macrophages, and polarize to M2.

substeps.instruction: Culture LNCaP prostate cancer cells and human THP‑1 monocytes in RPMI‑1640 medium supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum and 5 % antibiotics.
For stable EAF2 knockdown, infect LNCaP cells with LV‑EAF2‑RNAi or negative control (Genechem, CN) for 12 h, then select with puromycin (5 µg/mL) for one week.
Incubate the indicated cells in serum‑free medium for 48 h, collect the supernatant, and centrifuge to obtain conditioned media.
Differentiate THP‑1 cells into M0 macrophages by treating with phorbol myristate acetate (PMA, Sigma, USA) for 30 h.
Culture the M0 macrophages in the collected conditioned media (with or without EAF2 knockdown) for 3 days.
Add IL‑4 (20 ng/mL, MCE, CN) and IL‑13 (20 ng/mL, MCE, CN) to the M0 cultures to induce M2 polarization.

steps.title: Extract RNA and synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: Isolate total RNA with TRIzol, reverse‑transcribe to cDNA, and store for qPCR.

substeps.instruction: Extract total RNA from cells using TRIzol reagent (Invitrogen, USA).
Perform first‑strand cDNA synthesis using a kit from Promega (USA).

steps.title: Quantitative PCR
steps.instruction: Run real‑time PCR with SYBR Green using the listed primer pairs.

substeps.instruction: Prepare qPCR reactions with SYBR Green mix (Thermo Scientific, Waltham, USA).

Use the following primer sequences: EAF2 forward 5’-TTTGAAGTCATAGCGCACAGT-3’, reverse 5’-AATAGCGCAGCGGGATTCTC-3’; GAPDH forward 5’-CGACCACTTTGTCAAGCTCA-3’, reverse 5’-AGGGGAGATTCAGTGTGGTG-3’; MIF forward 5’-ATCGTAAACACCAACGTGCC-3’, reverse 5’-TTGCTGTAGGAGCGGTTCTG-3’; TNF‑α forward 5’-CCTCTCTCTAATCAGCCCTCTG-3’, reverse 5’-GAGGACCTGGGAGTAGATGAG-3’; IL‑6 forward 5’-ACTCACCTCTTCAGAACGAATTG-3’, reverse 5’-CCATCTTTGGAAGGTTCAGGTTG-3’; CD68 forward 5’-GGAAATGCCACGGTTCATCCA-3’, reverse 5’-TGGGGTTCAGTACAGAGATGC-3’; CD206 forward 5’-TCCGGGTGCTGTTCTCCTA-3’, reverse 5’-CCAGTCTGTTTTTGATGGCACT-3’; CD163 forward 5’-TTTGTCAACTTGAGTCCCTTCAC-3’, reverse 5’-TCCCGCTACACTTGTTTTCAC-3’; TGF‑β forward 5’-GGCCAGATCCTGTCCAAGC-3’, reverse 5’-GTGGGTTTCCACCATTAGCAC-3’.

steps.title: Prepare primer sequences
steps.instruction: Record the above primer sequences for use in qPCR assays.

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze experimental data with appropriate statistical tests and software, considering p < 0.05 as significant.

substeps.instruction: Present data as mean ± SEM.
Compare groups using Student’s t‑test or Chi‑square test as appropriate.
Calculate required sample size with the R package pwr (version 1.3‑0).
Perform analyses using SPSS 27.0 and GraphPad Prism 9.4.
Consider differences statistically significant when probability values are < 0.05.
